role: Retail and interconnection colocation REIT

role: Wholesale and hyperscale colocation REIT
note: Largest carrier-neutral wholesale landlord with 300+ data centers in 55+ metros and 30+ countries; develops hyperscale campuses partly through a $7B joint venture with Blackstone.

role: Hyperscale campus developer (DigitalBridge/Silver Lake-backed)

role: Hyperscale campus developer

role: AI data-center developer and neocloud

role: Bitcoin miner turned AI data-center landlord
note: 400 MW of critical IT leased to CoreWeave at Polaris Forge 1 (Ellendale, ND) under ~15-year leases worth about $11B in contracted revenue; the campus is engineered to scale to 1 GW.

role: Bitcoin miner converting sites to GPU hosting
note: Contracted to deliver approximately 500 MW of critical IT load to CoreWeave by H2 2026 under 12-year hosting contracts with $8.7B of projected cumulative revenue.

role: Bitcoin miner turned AI cloud and data-center operator
note: Signed a ~$9.7B five-year contract (20% prepaid) to give Microsoft access to GB300 GPUs at its 750 MW Childress, TX campus, housed in new liquid-cooled halls totalling 200 MW of critical IT (Horizon 1-4).

role: Bitcoin miner turned AI hosting landlord
note: Signed a ~$5.5B, 15-year lease with AWS for 300 MW delivered in two phases in 2026, on top of Fluidstack leases backstopped by Google; AI hosting contracts total about $8.5B.

role: Power and thermal equipment (UPS, switchgear, CDUs, chillers)
note: FY2025 net sales $10,229.9M with 26% organic growth, backlog $15.0B (+109%) and Q4 organic orders +252%; guides 2026 sales of $13.25-13.75B, the clearest public demand signal for data-center electrical and cooling gear.

role: Electrical distribution and cooling (Motivair liquid cooling)
note: Took a controlling interest in liquid-cooling specialist Motivair in Feb 2025 and now sells coolant distribution units from 105 kW to 2.5 MW alongside switchgear and UPS, positioning as 'grid to chip'.

role: Electrical equipment; liquid cooling via Boyd Thermal
note: Agreed in Nov 2025 to buy Boyd Thermal for $9.5B (Boyd expected 2026 sales $1.7B, $1.5B of it liquid cooling), closing expected Q2 2026; Eaton's own release timed out for the fetcher, so a secondary copy is cited.

role: Gas turbine and grid equipment maker
note: Largest gas turbine supplier; 116 GW of gas equipment backlog plus slot reservations at Q2 2026, with output of 20 GW/yr rising to a targeted 30 GW in 2030.

role: Gas turbine and grid equipment maker
note: Gas services backlog reached 69 GW at end-June 2026 after booking 15 GW of orders and shipping 6 GW in the quarter; the CFO says lead times now run three years or more.

role: Gas turbine maker
note: Large-frame gas turbine backlog of 35 GW (up from 23 GW a year earlier), plans to double production capacity versus 2024, and orders booked in mid-2026 are scheduled for 2028-2030 delivery.

role: Nuclear generator with hyperscaler PPAs
note: Restarting the 835 MW Crane (Three Mile Island 1) plant for 2027 and signed a 20-year deal with Meta for 1,121 MW from Clinton starting June 2027, including a 30 MW uprate.

role: Independent power producer (nuclear and gas)
note: 20-year PPA for 1,200 MW from Comanche Peak with delivery from late 2027, and Meta will buy more than 2.1 GW from its Perry and Davis-Besse nuclear plants with 433 MW of uprates due in the early 2030s.

role: Independent power producer (nuclear)
note: Supplying Amazon with 1,920 MW of nuclear power from Susquehanna through 2042, moving to a front-of-the-meter arrangement in spring 2026.

role: Utility and renewables/nuclear developer
note: Restarting the 615 MW Duane Arnold nuclear plant (closed 2020) by the first quarter of 2029 under a 25-year agreement with Google.

role: Independent power producer (gas)
note: Partnership with GE Vernova and Kiewit to build up to 5.4 GW of combined-cycle gas for data centres, 1.2 GW in service by 2029 and another 1.2 GW by 2030; total contracted data-centre capacity 445 MW as of November 2025.

role: On-site fuel-cell power for data centres
note: Says it can deliver on-site power for an entire data centre within 90 days and had deployed more than 400 MW at data centres by mid-2025; supplying Oracle Cloud Infrastructure sites.

role: Gas pipelines and behind-the-meter power
note: Completed phase one of Socrates, its first behind-the-meter gas plant for a data centre in Ohio, with phase two due 4Q 2026; formed a $5.34 billion Power Innovation joint venture with Blackstone and guides 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $8.3-8.5 billion.

role: Gas pipelines
note: $9.6 billion project backlog at end of Q2 2026, more than 60% tied to power generation and local distribution company demand.

role: Natural gas producer (Appalachia)
note: Signed a long-term supply agreement for a new 2 GW power plant in West Virginia and a 10-year deal to supply 325,000 Dth/d to the CPV Shay Energy Center at prices linked to PJM power.

role: Transformer and grid equipment maker
note: Announced more than $1 billion of US grid-equipment manufacturing investment in September 2025, including about $457 million for a new large power transformer plant in South Boston, Virginia, citing AI data-centre demand.

role: Transformers (Prolec GE), switchgear and grid systems
note: Electrification equipment backlog of $40.6 billion at Q2 2026, up 69% year on year including $5 billion from Prolec GE; data-centre orders topped $5 billion year-to-date, more than double all of 2025.

role: Transformers, switchgear and HVDC
note: Grid Technologies is one of the three main transformer suppliers to the US market; the Q3 FY2026 release (August 5, 2026) reports record order intake and raised revenue guidance for the group.

role: Transformers, switchgear and data-centre electrical equipment
note: Investing $340 million to raise US three-phase transformer output at a new Jonesville, South Carolina plant with production from 2027, in response to a shortage that has pushed utility transformer lead times to 120 weeks (Utility Dive, Feb 12, 2025).

role: Utility serving Northern Virginia data centres
note: Nearly 53.8 GW of data-centre capacity in contracting stages in Virginia as of July 2026, up 5.3 GW since December 2025.

role: Multi-state utility (PJM, SPP, ERCOT)
note: 69 GW of contracted load growth through 2030 as of Q2 2026 and a $78 billion five-year capital plan weighted to transmission.

role: Regional transmission organisation (13 states plus DC)
note: Largest US grid operator; its board in January 2026 defined large-load additions as 50 MW or more at a single point of interconnection and directed a voluntary Bring Your Own New Generation track plus a reliability backstop procurement.

role: Texas grid operator
note: Tracking about 410 GW of large-load requests (about 87% data centres) as of March 2026 and moving to a batch study process for loads of 75 MW and above with $50,000/MW financial security under the PUCT's proposed rule.

role: HBM leader; No. 2 DRAM; NAND (Solidigm)
note: Held 56.4% of HBM revenue in 1Q26 per IDC as cited in its own Nasdaq prospectus; Q2 2026 revenue KRW 79.3 trillion at a 76% operating margin, 2026 capex guided to the high KRW 40 trillion range.

role: Largest DRAM and NAND maker; HBM4 challenger
note: Largest DRAM supplier with $37.32 billion of 1Q26 DRAM revenue (TrendForce); its HBM revenue share rose from 21% to 33% in Q2 2026 per Counterpoint as HBM4 ramped.

role: No. 3 DRAM/HBM and NAND; only US memory maker
note: Fiscal Q3 2026 revenue $41.46 billion (75.6% DRAM); has shipped over $1 billion of HBM4, contracted all of its calendar 2026 HBM supply, and guides fiscal 2026 capex to about $27 billion.

role: NAND and enterprise SSD (Kioxia JV fabs)
note: Fiscal 2026 revenue $20.25 billion, up 175%, with two-thirds of Q4 sequential growth from pricing; the 2025 bottleneck case-study stock, up about five-fold across 2025.

role: NAND maker (Yokkaichi and Kitakami fabs, JV with Sandisk)
note: Quarter to June 2026 revenue JPY 1,767.1 billion, up 76.2% QoQ, on a roughly 70% rise in blended ASP with only low-single-digit bit growth; its CEO said in Sept 2026 that prices 'have already risen enough'.

role: Nearline HDD for cloud and AI data lakes
note: Fiscal Q4 2026 revenue $3.75 billion, up 44% year-over-year; fiscal 2026 revenue about $12.9 billion, up 36%, as AI data centers absorb high-capacity HDDs.

role: Nearline HDD; HAMR (Mozaic) density leader
note: Fiscal 2026 revenue $12.2 billion, up 34%, with Q4 revenue $3.6 billion; the other half of the HDD duopoly, citing 'strengthening exabyte demand' addressed through its Mozaic HAMR platform.

role: ALD and epitaxy tools for advanced DRAM/HBM
note: Q1 2026 revenue EUR 863 million; said memory demand 'was solid, largely for the most advanced DRAM device technologies used in HBM-related applications', with memory a smaller share than logic/foundry.

role: Etch and deposition; TSV etch and plating for HBM
note: Record March-2026-quarter revenue of $5.84 billion on AI-driven demand; a leader in the through-silicon-via etch and copper plating steps that stack HBM dies.

role: Deposition, CMP and packaging tools for DRAM/HBM
note: Record fiscal Q2 2026 revenue of $7.91 billion, up 11%; signed a long-term collaboration with SK hynix on next-generation DRAM and HBM and expects its semiconductor equipment business to grow more than 30% in calendar 2026.

role: Etch, coater/developer and wafer bonders for DRAM/HBM
note: Raising FY26 capex 48% to JPY 240 billion on DRAM interconnection (TSV) etch demand for HBM and targeting JPY 500 billion cumulative etch sales by fiscal 2030 (TrendForce citing Nikkei).

role: Thermal-compression (TC) bonders that stack HBM dies
note: Main TC bonder supplier to SK hynix; a June 2026 order for HBM4 TC bonders was worth KRW 44.2 billion, about 7.7% of Hanmi's 2025 revenue.

role: GPU and rack-scale system design (fabless)
note: Data Center revenue of $89.0 billion in the quarter ended July 26, 2026, up 117% year on year, with the Blackwell architecture 'the vast majority' of revenue and supply commitments of $279 billion; it buys wafers from TSMC and packaging on CoWoS.

role: GPU (Instinct) and server CPU (EPYC) design (fabless)
note: The only merchant GPU alternative at scale: Data Center segment revenue $6.7 billion in the quarter ended June 27, 2026, up 107%, driven by EPYC CPUs and Instinct MI350 GPUs; also fabs at TSMC.

role: Custom AI ASIC (XPU) design for hyperscalers plus Ethernet networking silicon
note: Largest custom-accelerator designer (Google TPU and other hyperscaler programs): AI semiconductor revenue of $16.7 billion in the quarter ended Aug. 2, 2026, up 221% year on year, with $21.7 billion guided for the next quarter.

role: Custom AI ASIC design and data-centre connectivity silicon
note: Second custom-silicon house for hyperscalers: quarterly revenue $2.739 billion in the quarter ended Aug. 1, 2026 with data-centre revenue up 46% year on year, and a custom-chip ramp it says begins in the second half of fiscal 2027.

role: Leading-edge foundry (N3, N2) and CoWoS advanced packaging
note: Makes essentially every AI accelerator in volume: Q2 2026 revenue US$40.20 billion with 3nm at 30% of wafer revenue, 2026 capex guided to US$60-64 billion, and reported CoWoS capacity of 120,000-140,000 wafers per month in 2026.

role: Second-source leading-edge foundry (2nm) with a US fab
note: The only other foundry shipping sub-3nm logic; its largest foundry win is a $16.5 billion Tesla AI6 contract running to end-2033 on its 2nm process at Taylor, Texas, and NVIDIA's 10-K names it alongside TSMC as a wafer supplier.

role: US-based foundry (18A in volume, 14A in development) and advanced packaging (EMIB, Foveros)
note: The would-be third leading-edge foundry: Intel Foundry revenue $5.8 billion in Q2 2026 (up 31%, mostly internal) with an operating loss of $2,089 million; 18A is in high-volume manufacturing for Panther Lake and 18A-P entered risk production, but external AI-accelerator volume is not yet proven.

role: Sole supplier of EUV lithography tools that every leading-edge fab needs
note: Gates how fast N3/N2/18A capacity can be added: Q2 2026 net sales EUR 9.3 billion, 2026 low-NA EUV capacity of around 65 systems with a 30% addition planned for 2027, and 2026 sales guided to EUR 43-45 billion.

role: Custom ASIC design services (TSMC ecosystem) for hyperscaler accelerators
note: Design-services partner behind AWS's Trainium 3: the 3nm chip was reported to enter mass production in Q2 2026, and Alchip says several 2nm AI and HPC projects are under way.

role: Custom ASIC design services and turnkey manufacturing; TSMC affiliate
note: TSMC's in-house-adjacent design house for custom silicon (HBM and UCIe IP, advanced packaging); reported to have secured next-generation CPU projects from Google and Meta, and ASIC-based servers are forecast at 27.8% of AI server shipments in 2026.

role: Wafer-scale AI accelerator design (WSE-3) and inference cloud
note: The main non-GPU, non-ASIC architecture at scale: 2025 revenue of about $510 million (S-1 table: 509,991 in thousands, versus 290,252 in 2024) and a multi-year OpenAI deal worth more than $20 billion for 750 MW of compute; its WSE-3 is a single chip '58 times larger than NVIDIA's B200'.

role: LPU inference accelerator design
note: Inference-specialist chip designer whose technology NVIDIA agreed in December 2025 to license for nearly $20 billion while hiring CEO Jonathan Ross and senior engineers; the deal has since drawn antitrust scrutiny (Bloomberg, Sept. 2026, paywalled).

role: largest AI server and NVL72 rack assembler (ODM/EMS)
note: Q2 2026 revenue reached NT$2.53 trillion; the company said full-year AI rack shipments 'are also expected to more than double', with Vera Rubin racks entering mass production in Q3 2026, and secondary coverage put cloud and networking at 51% of revenue, passing half for the first time.

role: AI server ODM for hyperscalers (GB200/GB300 racks, custom-ASIC servers)
note: Servers were 80% of Q1 2026 revenue of NT$809.22 billion and AI servers 75% of server revenue, but gross margin fell to 4.78%, showing how thin ODM margins are on NVIDIA rack systems.

role: hyperscale server and rack ODM (Wistron group)
note: Q1 2026 consolidated revenue of NT$276.508 billion, up 62.0% year on year, with profit after tax of NT$14.114 billion; one of the four ODMs building GB200/GB300 NVL72 racks.

role: AI server and liquid-cooled rack OEM (Data Center Building Block Solutions)
note: Fiscal 2026 net sales of $39.1 billion (up from $22.0 billion), Q4 net sales $11.1 billion, more than $60 billion of new orders in the year and fiscal 2027 guidance of $65.0-72.0 billion.

role: AI server OEM (PowerEdge XE, NVL72 racks) for enterprises and neoclouds
note: Booked $60.9 billion of AI server orders and recognised $16.4 billion of AI server revenue in the quarter ended 31 Jul 2026, with a $95 billion AI backlog; traditional servers and networking revenue was $10.5 billion, up 122%.

role: AI systems and server OEM (Cray, ProLiant, GB200 NVL72 by HPE), plus Juniper networking
note: Fiscal Q3 2026 (quarter to 31 Jul 2026) revenue of $12.2 billion, up 34%, with Server revenue of $6.8 billion, up 35.3%, and order backlog 'at a record level'; HPE's own spec sheet rates the GB200 NVL72 rack at 132 kW.

role: Ethernet switching for AI back-end and front-end networks
note: Q2 2026 revenue of $3.036 billion, up 37.7% year on year and its first $3 billion quarter, with Q3 guided to about $3.3 billion and new 1.6 Tbps liquid-cooled AI fabric platforms; does not disclose AI revenue separately.

role: Ethernet switching, optics and Silicon One for hyperscaler AI back-end networks
note: Took $4 billion of hyperscaler AI-infrastructure orders in fiscal Q4 2026, bringing fiscal 2026 to $9.3 billion, delivered about $4 billion of AI-infrastructure revenue in FY2026 and expects $7.5 billion in FY2027; networking product orders grew 40% in Q4.

role: Ethernet switch silicon (Tomahawk/Jericho), optics and custom AI accelerators
note: AI semiconductor revenue of $16.7 billion in fiscal Q3 2026 (up 221%), guided to $21.7 billion in Q4; the release says demand for custom AI accelerators and networking 'continues to be very strong'.

role: optical transceivers (800G/1.6T) and lasers for AI data centres
note: Fiscal Q4 2026 (quarter to 30 Jun 2026) revenue of $2.05 billion, up 34% year on year, with Datacenter & Communications revenue of $1,615.0 million and Q1 FY2027 guided to $2.2-2.4 billion; peers Lumentum ($1.01 billion, up 109.3%) and Credo ($479.0 million, up 114.7%) grew faster from smaller bases.

role: power distribution, thermal and liquid-cooling (CDUs) for AI racks
note: Backlog of $15.0 billion at end-2025 (up 109%) against 2026 sales guidance of $14,000 million; Q2 2026 net sales $3,274 million, up 24%; co-developed with NVIDIA a 7 MW GB200 NVL72 reference design at 'up to 132kW per rack'. Main rival Schneider Electric (Motivair) sells CDUs from 105 kW to 2.5 MW.

role: direct-to-chip cold plates and CDUs for GPU servers and NVL72 racks
note: Ecolab agreed on 20 Mar 2026 to pay approximately $4.75 billion in cash for CoolIT, which is expected to generate approximately $550 million in sales over the following 12 months, implying about 8.6x sales for a cold-plate and CDU maker; closing expected in Q3 2026.
